title: Writing a simple song
examples: What is the difference between a verse and a chorus?
How do I make a song sound more interesting?
Can a song have more than one chorus?

explain.say: Today we are learning about writing a simple song structure.
A verse tells a story and usually has different lyrics each time.

items: End: Moving to the next part

explain.say: The chorus is the main part that repeats throughout the whole song.
A bridge offers a change in mood or perspective from the rest.

draw.text: Bridge: Change of pace or thought

explain.say: A hook is a short, catchy part designed to stick in your head.
The lyrics are all the words you sing in the song.

faq.q: What is the difference between a verse and a chorus?
faq.a: The verse tells a specific part of the story, while the chorus is the main message that repeats.
asks: Why does the chorus sound different from the verse?
Should the verse always be about a different topic?

faq.q: How long should a bridge be in a song?
faq.a: A bridge should be long enough to feel like a change but not so long that it loses momentum.
asks: Does the bridge have to be a different melody?
Can I skip the bridge if I want a shorter song?

faq.q: What is the purpose of a hook?
faq.a: The hook is designed to be the most memorable part, making people want to sing along.
asks: Is the hook the same as the chorus?
Should the hook always be sung at the beginning?

faq.q: Do I need to write lyrics for every part?
faq.a: Yes, the lyrics provide the words for every section, including the verse, chorus, and bridge.
asks: Can I just use rhyming words for the lyrics?
Do the lyrics need to match the rhythm?

faq.a: Song structure is the plan that organizes the different parts of your song together.
asks: Is structure the same as rhythm?
Do I need to plan the structure before writing?

facts: A song structure uses different parts to keep the listener interested.
The chorus usually contains the song's main theme or message.
A bridge provides a temporary break from the main musical pattern.
A hook is a short, catchy musical or lyrical phrase.

quiz.say: If you are telling a story about a trip to the beach, which section should describe arriving at the sand?
quiz.why: The verse is where you tell the specific details of your story, like arriving at the sand.

wrong.1: The chorus is for the main, repeating feeling, not the story details.
wrong.2: The bridge is for a change of thought, not the main action of the story.
wrong.3: The hook is just a short, catchy phrase, not the whole story part.

quiz.say: Which part of a song is meant to be the most memorable and catchy?
quiz.why: The hook is specifically designed to be the part that gets stuck in your head.

wrong.1: The verse focuses on moving the story forward with details.
wrong.2: While catchy, the chorus is the main idea, not necessarily the single catchiest part.
wrong.3: The bridge's job is to change things up, not necessarily to be the catchiest part.

quiz.say: A song goes: Verse, Chorus, Verse, Chorus, Bridge, Chorus. What is the purpose of the Bridge in this structure?

options.show: To change the mood or perspective
options.say: To change the mood or perspective

quiz.why: The bridge breaks the pattern to give the listener a musical or lyrical change before returning to the main chorus.

wrong.1: Repeating the story is the job of the verse.
wrong.2: Introducing a whole new story is too much for just one section.
wrong.3: Repeating the main message is the job of the chorus.
